teaser.en: Its Digo name means simply 'bitter vegetable', and that bitterness is part of why it ends up both in the pot and in medicine.
teaser.sw: Jina lake la Kidigo lina maana tu ya 'mboga chungu', na uchungu huo ni sehemu ya sababu ya kuishia chunguni na pia kwenye dawa.

summary.en: *Mtsunga wa utsungu* is wild lettuce, a milky-sapped herb of farmland and grassland. Its bitter leaves are cooked as greens and used in medicine.
summary.sw: *Mtsunga wa utsungu* ni mchunga, mmea wenye utomvu mweupe kama maziwa unaoota mashambani na mbugani. Majani yake machungu hupikwa kama mboga na hutumika kama dawa.

about.en: *Mtsunga wa utsungu* is a herb with long, deeply lobed leaves. Break a leaf and a milky sap runs out. The small yellow flower heads look like dandelions, to which it is related.
about.sw: *Mtsunga wa utsungu* ni mmea wenye majani marefu yenye pindo za kina. Ukivunja jani, utomvu mweupe kama maziwa hutoka. Vichwa vyake vidogo vya maua ya manjano vinafanana na vya *dandelion*, ambaye ni jamaa yake.

where.en: It grows on farmland, fallows and grassland, and is common as a farm weed.
where.sw: Huota mashambani, kwenye mashamba yaliyoachwa yapumzike na mbugani, na ni gugu la kawaida shambani.

uses.en: The bitter leaves are cooked as greens. The leaves are also used medicinally: the Digo of Diani boil them as a remedy for malaria.
uses.sw: Majani yake machungu hupikwa kama mboga. Majani hayo pia hutumika kama dawa: Wadigo wa Diani huyachemsha kutibu malaria.

names.en: The Digo name *mtsunga wa utsungu* means 'bitter vegetable': *mtsunga* is the Digo word for vegetables, especially amaranths. The name is shared with Duruma and Giriama. Swahili calls it *mchunga*. In English it is wild lettuce or bitter lettuce.
names.sw: Jina la Kidigo *mtsunga wa utsungu* lina maana ya 'mboga chungu': *mtsunga* ni neno la Kidigo kwa mboga, hasa michicha. Jina hili linatumika pia kwa Kiduruma na Kigiriama. Kwa Kiswahili huitwa *mchunga*. Kwa Kiingereza huitwa *wild lettuce* au *bitter lettuce*.
